requirement:
`OutlineContent::language()` returns the name of the `OutlineLang` that produced
the snapshot. The root and each selected item report the same name. An explicit
provider supplies its own name, including when the filename would select a
different language by default.
rationale:
The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.language`.

- **Default languages.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[default_language_names_match_the_retained_outline]` builds roots with `OutlineContent::from_source` for `LIB.RS`, `widget.TSX`, `README` and `foo.unknown`. It asserts `root.language()` is `rust`, `tsx`, `plain-text` and `plain-text` respectively. It also asserts that `languages::name_for_path` returns the same names. The mixed-case extensions and the unknown-extension and no-extension fallbacks are covered.
- **Explicit provider overrides the filename.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]` supplies a `CustomLanguage` named `custom` with the misleading filename `misleading.rs`. It loads the root through both `from_source_with` and `from_path_with`, and asserts `root.language() == "custom"` for each. The default for `.rs` would be `rust`, so this checks that the provider's own name wins.
- **Selected item reports the same name.** The same test calls `supplied.select("part[selected]")` and asserts `selected.language() == "custom"`. That matches the root's name.

One gap is theoretical: no test selects an item from a default-language outline and checks its `language()`. The requirement does not distinguish selection by language source, and the selected-item check with an explicit provider exercises the same obligation, so I don't count it as a gap. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.
